Free-tuition & funded med schools — the endgame that erases the biggest billPlan for it

NYU Grossman (New York) — full tuition for every MD student since 2018; also runs a 3-year MD. NYU Grossman Long Island — tuition-free, 3-year, primary-care focused. Albert Einstein (Bronx) — tuition-free for all since 2024 ($1B Gottesman gift). Johns Hopkins — free tuition for families under ~$300k income, plus living costs under ~$175k (Bloomberg gift, 2024). Cleveland Clinic Lerner (CWRU) — full-tuition scholarship, 5-year research MD. Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson (Pasadena, CA) — waived tuition for its first five classes only; verify what applies to a 2031 entrant. Debt-free by need at Columbia, Harvard (families under ~$100k), WashU (free tuition for roughly half the class), and others. MD-PhD / MSTP anywhere — tuition paid + ~$45k/yr stipend, at the price of 4 extra years (the True Cost tab has a toggle for it).

Selectivity reality: these are the hardest med schools in the country to enter — NYU admits ~2% with a median MCAT ~522 and GPA ~3.95; Einstein’s applications roughly doubled after going free. They are a target to aim at, never a plan to count on. Set the med-school slider on the True Cost tab to ~$17k/yr (living only) to see what landing one does to the ledger.

The plan that gets there (or to any strong MD program)4-year checklist

1. GPA 3.8+ in college — the single biggest lever. Choose an undergrad where a high GPA is achievable for him, not the most prestigious one that will grade him down (a 3.9 from SDSU or UC Davis beats a 3.4 from Berkeley at every med-school screen). Grade-deflation notes are on each card in The List.

2. MCAT 518+ — plan a dedicated 4–6 month prep block (summer after junior year) and take it once, well prepared. Free-tuition schools sit at 519–522.

3. Keep the research thread alive — his Parkinson’s-biomarker manuscript is a rare asset for a high-schooler; a 4-year lab home with a second paper or poster is what those committees look for. Pick a campus where a median premed gets a lab by sophomore year (Research access column).

4. Clinical continuity — 100+ hours is already there; add depth (one long-term role: scribe, EMT, hospice) over breadth. Clinical column tells you where that is easy.

5. Apply broadly and early — the free-tuition schools are lottery tickets on top of a real list: CA publics first (UC Davis / Irvine / Riverside / UCSD are the cheapest MD seats a Californian can get), then 3-year MD pathways as a cost cut, then the MSTP route if the research love is real.

6. Early assurance from inside college — FlexMed (any college, no MCAT, sophomore year) and the school-specific EAPs on the green cards below are the realistic version of a "direct pathway" at his band.

Accelerated 6- and 7-year programs (UMKC, Howard, California Northstate 3+4, Penn State–Jefferson, RPI–Albany and the rest) now have their own tab — Accelerated — with entry bars, restrictions, and full cost through the ledger. Boston University’s SMED has closed and was removed from the roster below.
